The proposed answer of 70° is wrong. A direct coordinate computation gives 55°.

**Setup.** Put the center O of Ω at the origin with r₁ along the positive x-axis, and let R be the radius of Ω. The center P of ω lies on the bisector, the ray at 20°, so P = (d cos 20°, d sin 20°) with d = OP.

**Radius of ω.** Let ρ be the radius of ω. Tangency to r₁ gives ρ = d sin 20°. Internal tangency to Ω gives d = R − ρ. Solving, ρ = R sin 20° / (1 + sin 20°).

**Points.** B is the foot of the perpendicular from P to r₁, so B = (d cos 20°, 0). A lies on ray OP at distance R from O, so A = (R cos 20°, R sin 20°). C = (R, 0).

**Angle.** BC points in the +x direction. The vector BA = ((R − d) cos 20°, R sin 20°) = (ρ cos 20°, R sin 20°). Therefore

tan∠ABC = R sin 20° / (ρ cos 20°) = (1 + sin 20°) / cos 20° = tan(45° + 10°) = tan 55°.

So ∠ABC = 55°.

The proposed solution never derived its value. It only asserted 70° after stating "we can show," so the answer 70 is incorrect.

VERDICT: REJECT
